title: Small Comforts by the River
paras: While sorting family papers, I found two very different accounts of Leila Haddad's first year abroad. Leila was a tea [[importer|importer]] who had rented a warehouse beside a river. Her account book listed deliveries and payments. Her letters described the [[steep|steep]] steps down to the water, where she often sat alone after work.

Those letters offer an [[insight|insight]] into difficulties the account book barely mentions. Leila struggled to speak with her neighbours and feared that moving abroad would [[deprive|deprive]] her of friendship. Then a baker invited her to a weekly gathering on the [[riverside|riverside]]. People brought bread and tea, borrowing chairs from nearby shops. It was ordinary [[recreation|recreation]], not a grand celebration.

When relatives ask why these meetings mattered, I [[cite|cite]] a letter about an evening when Leila hardly spoke. She remembered picking a [[crumb|crumb]] from her sleeve while listening to the others talk. Their quiet [[presence|presence]], she wrote, mattered more than anything they said. By the following week, she was bringing extra cups for anyone who might join them.

Later, the baker injured his hand and could not work. Leila organised a collection for him, keeping the coins in a small tin box. She described this [[deed|deed]] simply as returning a kindness. In her account book, between two tea deliveries, I found the amount collected and a note confirming that he had received it.
zh: 整理家里的旧文件时，我发现了两种截然不同的记录，都讲述了莱拉·哈达德在国外的第一年。莱拉是一位茶叶进口商，在河边租了一间仓库。她的账本列着送货和收付款记录。她的信则描写了通向水边的陡峭台阶，她常在下班后独自坐在那里。
这些信让我们深入了解了账本几乎没有提及的困境。莱拉与邻居交谈时感到吃力，担心移居国外会让自己失去友谊。后来，一位面包师邀请她参加每周在河畔举行的聚会。大家带来面包和茶，从附近的店铺借来椅子。这是日常消遣，而非盛大的庆典。
亲人问起这些聚会为何重要时，我会引用一封信，信里写的是莱拉几乎没有说话的一个晚上。她记得，自己一边听其他人交谈，一边从袖子上拈起一粒面包屑。她写道，比起他们说了什么，更重要的是他们安静地陪伴在身旁。到了下一周，她已开始多带一些杯子，供可能加入的人使用。
后来，面包师伤了手，无法工作。莱拉为他组织了一次募捐，把硬币放在一个小铁盒里。对于这一善举，她只说是在回报一份善意。在她的账本上，两笔茶叶送货记录之间，我找到了募集的金额，还有一条确认他已经收款的备注。

q.s: Leila's letters reveal difficulties that her account book barely mentions.
q.why: 第二段明确说信件揭示账本几乎未提的困境。

q.s: The weekly riverside gatherings were grand celebrations.
q.why: 原文说这是日常消遣，而非盛大庆典。

q.s: The money collected for the baker covered all his lost earnings.
q.why: 文章未说明募款是否弥补了全部收入损失。
